_comment: Why this exists: `transcoding-service` was running on MINIO_ROOT_USER. That is
the full-storage takeover credential, in the one service that reads every
user's source video and writes HLS renditions - so it is the single highest
blast radius service in the stack, and it had the widest key.
The gap table in `updatedtodo.md` marked 'MinIO uses root credentials' as
CLOSED. That was true for auth-service, which got `wideo11-auth-avatars`, and
false here. A fix applied to four services out of five is not a fix.
Scope is deliberately narrower than auth-avatars:
- READ on `video/*`    - it has to fetch the source file to transcode it
- WRITE on `video/*`   - it writes HLS segments and playlists
- NOTHING on `avatars` - it has no business touching a profile image
No `s3:DeleteBucket`, no `s3:PutBucketPolicy`, no admin actions. It can only
read and write objects inside the one bucket it needs.
Note the READ grant covers `video/*`, which includes other users' uploads.
That is unavoidable - a transcode reads arbitrary source files - and it is why
the service still must not be reachable by anything untrusted.
